what_happened: Task description's two candidate causes (stdin read in a non-interactive context; unbounded Zotero API/socket wait) were both refuted by a full read of zotero-generate-export.sh and zotero-resolve-sqlite-path.sh: no bare stdin read exists anywhere, and every curl call carries --connect-timeout/--max-time. Actual root cause (confirmed by microbenchmark N=50..2000 showing superlinear growth, and a live uncontended rerun of the failing short-mid-page scenario completing in ~122s) is synthesize_citekeys()'s per-item bash for-loop: each of its ~2828 iterations re-parses the full, growing items_json via a fresh jq subprocess AND re-serializes the full, growing result array via another fresh jq subprocess, giving O(n) subprocess spawns each doing O(n) JSON work -- effectively quadratic wall-clock cost, not a deadlock. Under the isolated timeout 60/90 reproduction this reads as 'stalls past the timeout' (it is killed mid-run, well short of its ~122s uncontended completion time); under the 24-minute concurrent-batch observation (load avg ~40/24 cores) the same mechanism is amplified by severe CPU-scheduling contention across thousands of short-lived jq child processes.
